title: No more fishes: Plants as a bio-factory for omega-3 fatty acid
content: The benefits of omega-3 (ω-3) fatty acids, which include α-linolenic acid (ALA), eicosapentaenoic acid, and docosahexaenoic acid (DHA), for human health are well known. They are essential for controlling obesity, cholesterol levels, cancer onset, and inflammation. One of the known sources for omega-3 fatty acids is deep-sea fishes and fish-derived oils. However, dietary constraints, limited supply, cost, and rigid isolation processes have forced us to explore other natural sources for omega-3 fatty acids. Plants could be an alternative and sustainable source for ALA. Plants produce ALA by desaturation of oleic acid, mediated by omega-3 fatty acid desaturase (FAD), a crucial enzyme that determines ALA content.
